purpose: 271 ORIGINAL NativeZipper executions of the reused eight-state eraser. All words of lengths0..7 and four patterns each at widths8,17,64,128. Check halt at label0,absolute head restored at varying negative positions,and every literal residual zipper cell blank,including both former START/STOP markers. The kernel-checked denotation theorem identifies this residual all-blank zipper with the actual blank infinite tape. This tests the erase subroutine,not its future integration into the joint-endpoint caller.
source:
import TransposeFollowup.NativeErase
open TransposeFollowup FixedTapeCompiler

def bits (m n : Nat) : List Bool := (List.range m).map n.testBit

def checkErase (m n : Nat) : Bool :=
  let xs := bits m n
  let pos : Fin 1 → Int := fun _ => ((n%23 : Nat) : Int)-57
  let c := NativeZipper.run NativeErase.program (4*m+4) (NativeErase.cfg 2 (Counter.marked xs) pos)
  decide (c.core.pc=0) && decide (c.pos 0=pos 0) &&
    decide ((c.core.tapes 0).left=[CopyMachine.Sym.blank]) &&
    decide ((c.core.tapes 0).right=List.replicate (m+1) CopyMachine.Sym.blank)

def checks : Nat × Nat := Id.run do
  let mut count := 0
  let mut failures := 0
  for m in List.range 8 do
    for n in List.range (2^m) do
      count := count+1
      if !checkErase m n then failures := failures+1
  for m in [8,17,64,128] do
    for n in [0,1,2^m-1,(2^m-1)/3] do
      count := count+1
      if !checkErase m n then failures := failures+1
  return (count,failures)
#eval checks
